hypothesis: Deriving expected AST operands with old operands masked can reduce anchoring on stale assertions. Whole-test review remains required. No model request contains native outcomes.
normalization: Deduplicate complete source-only rankings by first occurrence; this rule was chosen after inspecting format errors, before detection labels.
source_pool: Previously generated pure program candidates. This is incremental reuse, not cold-start generation.
tests: 10 focused tests passed; input immutability, exact slot filling, call rejection, identity semantics, normalization, and context allowlisting.
report_policy: At most one alert per trial, first supported native failure. Audit every alert independently. Keep all 17 trials in the denominator.
promotion: Not promoted. Conservative F1=4/27 versus round01 8/29. This comparison includes every emitted alert and all 17 trials.
conclusions: Masking the direct operand leaves oracle-only constants visible and does not prevent stale-constant anchoring.
Source-only candidate rankings omit many previously known witnesses; stronger expectation filling cannot recover omitted inputs.
Whole-test review still admits API misuse, loader failures, invalid protocol defaults and stale structural observers.
Candidate execution failure and whole-test validity must remain separate evidence.
